topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
response: The 0.25 dB passband loss would reduce the link budget margin by approximately 0.25 dB, assuming a linear relationship between loss and margin. This reduction is due to the decrease in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the receiver frontend. In a low-noise satellite receiver, this loss would be more pronounced, potentially leading to a 0.25 dB decrease in the EIRP (Effective Isotropic Radiated Power) or a 0.25 dB increase in the noise figure.
